numerical_characteristics.magnitude: decision_function returns large negative values for every class of a single input; exp(-1000) = 0 in floating point, so all OvR probabilities become zero and the normalization divides by zero producing NaN or inf
category_specific_evidence: Expected property: predicted probabilities for each sample should sum to 1 (OvR normalization divides each row by its sum), but when all class probabilities are zero in floating point the row sum is 0 and the division yields NaN/inf.
Concrete violating value: exp(-1000) = 0 in floating point, given in the PR body as the example that zeroes all probabilities.
Fix behavior: rows whose probability sum is zero are set to uniform probabilities (prob = 1 per class, sum set to n_classes), so each row normalizes to 1/n_classes per class.
Issue #17978 reports predict_proba() returning NaNs for linear models with log loss when training yields large coefficients, with the normalization in _predict_proba_lr dividing by zero.
Reported reproduction context: SGDClassifier with log loss and default alpha, trained in minibatches; the NaN surfaced as ValueError: Input contains NaN in check_array.
New test test_predict_proba_lr_large_values tests that _predict_proba_lr handles large negative values; its body is not included in the passages.
Whats_new entry states equal probability is assigned for each class in the multiclass case where large negative decision_function values cause NaN.
reproduction_risks: Exact dtype, precision and numeric tolerance used by the test are not stated in the passages.
The exact coefficient or decision_function values that trigger the failure are not given; the issue's gist data is referenced but not included.
The fix applies only to the multiclass OvR branch; the binary branch is not shown changed in the diff excerpt.
The PR body says the only estimator affected is probably SGDClassifier, but this is stated as uncertain by the author.
